title: Drafting a winning injunction application - the key elements
p1:
A weak injunction application can lose before the real dispute even begins.

Many believe the strongest argument wins, but courts often look first at something else: whether the application clearly shows why immediate protection is needed.
p2:
A common mistake is treating an injunction request like a detailed version of the main case. In reality, it is about urgency, balance, and preventing harm that may be difficult to undo later.

The key is connecting the facts with the risk. A court needs to see what harm may happen, why waiting is dangerous, and why the requested protection is reasonable.
p3:
A well-drafted injunction application usually focuses on three things: a clear right that needs protection, a genuine risk of damage, and a practical solution that does not unfairly affect the other side.

The strongest applications do not just ask for an order — they explain why the order is necessary at that moment.
conclusion: What do you think makes an injunction application persuasive: strong legal arguments, clear facts, or proving urgency?
